use_case: Process-optimization model recommending caustic feed ratio and temperature setpoints for the Plant C1 hypochlorite reactors
vendor_or_model: In-house gradient-boosted model on provider A managed machine learning (SYS-C9)
data_categories: Historian data (temperatures, flows, ratios, analyzer results); batch records; no personal data (Restricted-Formulation)
affects_individuals: Yes (workers and the community if a setpoint contributed to a release)
consequential_decision_category: None about people; physical safety of a chemical process (repository rubric: affects physical safety or critical infrastructure operations)
human_in_the_loop: Advisory only since 2026-09-03: operators see recommendations and enter any change by hand. From 2026-06 to 2026-09-03 it wrote setpoints automatically within bounded ranges without MOC
applicable_laws: EPA RMP 40 CFR 68.65(c)(1)(iv), 68.69, 68.75 (Program 3); OSHA PSM 29 CFR 1910.119; RBPS 8 (voluntary); CISA-led joint guidance on AI in OT (2025-12-03, voluntary)
status: In production in advisory mode with conditions; automatic mode prohibited

vendor_or_model: Vendor condition-monitoring platform with machine learning models
data_categories: Vibration and temperature data; work orders; no personal data
human_in_the_loop: Recommendations create work requests; inspection and test frequencies for covered processes do not change without MOC
applicable_laws: EPA RMP 40 CFR 68.73(d) (frequencies per good engineering practice); vendor contract

use_case: Generative formulation assistant suggesting starting formulations for new cleaning products
business_owner: Specialty Chemicals Director of Process Control Engineering
vendor_or_model: Hosted large language model from a model provider, with a retrieval index of approved formulations
human_in_the_loop: Chemists review every suggestion; nothing reaches a plant without lab trials, a compatibility check, and MOC
applicable_laws: Trade secret protection (contract: no training on inputs, limited retention); EPA RMP 68.65(b)(7) and 68.75 if a suggestion becomes a change to a covered process
status: Pilot (2 product teams); expansion paused until terms are verified

use_case: Driver-facing camera AI that scores events (distraction, drowsiness, phone use) and feeds coaching and discipline
business_owner: Hazmat Transport Vice President of Safety and Compliance
data_categories: In-cab video and images of drivers; event scores; driver identifiers (Restricted-Personal)
human_in_the_loop: Today: scores reach terminal managers, who discipline without a documented review of the video. Required from 2026-11-30: a trained reviewer watches every clip before any discipline, and the score is never the sole basis
applicable_laws: State AI employment laws for drivers living in those states: Illinois HB 3773 (effective 2026-01-01, notice and anti-discrimination), Colorado SB26-189 (from 2027-01-01, consequential employment decisions), California CPPA ADMT rules (compliance by 2027-01-01, under counsel review); Title VII disparate impact; state biometric privacy laws if the vendor uses facial geometry (under counsel review)
status: In production with conditions (coaching continues; discipline only after documented human review)
